scope: Read-only structural/editorial survey, not classification validation. Screen headings containing comma, semicolon, ampersand, or word and that have children. Counts are headings, not unique branches; depth is shortest root distance. No taxonomy changes. Prior three upper-hierarchy proposals explicitly declined. Recommendations are review directions, not approved mutations.

reviewed.label: Recreation, Travel & Adventure
reviewed.review_note: Children’s nonfiction grouping includes Mathematics, Paranormal & Supernatural and Espionage alongside activities and travel. Review outliers and divide coherent branches; retain audience context.

reviewed.label: Art & Furniture Collectibles
reviewed.review_note: Fourteen collectible classes include bottles, buttons, kitchenware and textiles. Retain a substantial grouping, but broaden its name or divide by object type.

reviewed.label: AI, Data & Emerging Computing
reviewed.review_note: AI, data science and media processing are combined with a changing emerging-computing category. Review separate AI/data and computing-paradigm groupings.

reviewed.label: IT Applications & Management
reviewed.review_note: Software types, database management, IT auditing and general IT share a heading. Review applications versus IT management scopes.

reviewed.label: Learning, Reference & Society
reviewed.review_note: Learning, reference, careers, history and social aspects are combined. Review separate learning/careers and history/society scopes; check reference code placement.

reviewed.label: Artists & Art Institutions
reviewed.review_note: Artists and institutions share a branch with business, economics and forgeries. Review artist-focused versus art-market/institutional scopes.

reviewed.label: Family, Population & Gender
reviewed.review_note: Demography, migration, geography, family, gender, life stages and lifestyle share one heading. Review internal organization; preserve useful family/gender/life-stage groupings.

reviewed.label: Optics, Imaging & Acoustics
reviewed.review_note: Optics and imaging sit with acoustics and general sensors. Review distinct optics/imaging and acoustics placement, with sensor scope checked separately.

reviewed.label: Arts, Media & Story Forms
reviewed.review_note: YA art subjects, literary forms, humor and media tie-ins are grouped together. Review subject versus story-form organization without mixing audiences.

reviewed.label: History, People, Media & Reference
reviewed.review_note: Cooking history, chefs, essays, media tie-ins and collectibles are combined. Review subgroups and potential overlapping history nodes; no equivalence assumed.

reviewed.label: History, Biography & Community
reviewed.review_note: Both direct children are Jewish-history subjects. Check codes and descendants before considering a narrower History of Judaism label.

reviewed.label: Germanic & Nordic
reviewed.review_note: Countries and language labels are combined. Review whether membership follows language, place, or both, preserving useful regional navigation.

reviewed.label: Uralic & Basque
reviewed.review_note: Basque is bundled with Uralic-labelled language groups. Review source scope and the existing separate Uralic Languages grouping before proposing any split.

reviewed.label: Culture, Media & Belief
reviewed.review_note: Cultural sociology, media, religion, conspiracy theories and secret societies share one substantial branch. Review outliers, not wholesale removal.

reviewed.label: Wood, Metal, Glass & Ceramics
reviewed.review_note: Wood, metal, glass and ceramics form a recognizable crafts grouping, though the label is a list. Keep structure unless a better subdivision is demonstrated.

reviewed.label: People, Society & History
reviewed.review_note: An eight-child children’s nonfiction society/humanities grouping. Punctuation alone is not a reason to flatten.

reviewed.label: Fiber, Needlework & Sewing
reviewed.review_note: Fiber crafts, needlework and sewing are related practices; retain substantial branch.

reviewed.label: Accounting & Tax
reviewed.review_note: Accounting, bookkeeping and taxation form a useful business grouping despite only three children.
